artworks.title: Phoroneus, or Legislation
artworks.description: Hexagonal marble relief from the south face of Giotto's Campanile in Florence: Phoroneus personifies Legislation among the liberal arts and human inventions. Medieval Florence casts the Argive first-man — son of Inachus, teacher of fire and law in Pausanias — as the inventor who brings statute to humankind.

popCulture.title: Description of Greece
popCulture.creator: Pausanias
popCulture.description: Pausanias preserves Argive memory of Phoroneus as the first man and first king of the land, with a tomb and cult at Argos — Inachus' son as culture-hero of the Peloponnese.

popCulture.title: Phoroneus
popCulture.description: Primeval king of Argos, son of the river Inachus — father of Niobe of Argos and Apis in the early Argive king-lists.

popCulture.title: Inachus
popCulture.description: River-god of Argos and father of Phoroneus — the watery stem of the oldest Argive dynasty.

popCulture.title: Argos
popCulture.description: The city whose earliest remembered king is Phoroneus — Argive antiquity measured from Inachus' son.
